content: Due to the extensive length of the original text, I will provide a representative selection of rewritten interactions. 1. Chloroquine increases the levels or effects of methamphetamine by inhibiting the metabolism mediated by the hepatic enzyme CYP2D6. Exercise caution and monitor the patient closely. 2. Chloroquine elevates the levels or effects of metoprolol by interfering with CYP2D6-mediated hepatic metabolism. Careful monitoring is advised. 3. Chloroquine enhances the levels or effects of mexiletine by altering CYP2D6 hepatic enzyme activity. Use caution and monitor the patient. 4. Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of chloroquine by inhibiting CYP3A4-mediated hepatic and intestinal metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 5. Mirabegron raises the levels or effects of chloroquine by affecting CYP2D6 hepatic metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 6. Mitotane reduces chloroquine levels by inducing CYP3A4-mediated hepatic and intestinal metabolism. Mitotane is a strong inducer of CYP3A4, and dosage adjustments may be required when co-administered with CYP3A4 substrates. Monitor closely. 7. Chloroquine increases the levels or effects of morphine by inhibiting CYP2D6 hepatic metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient. 8. Chloroquine increases the toxicity of moxifloxacin by prolonging the QTc interval. Exercise caution and monitor the patient. 9. Chloroquine raises the levels or effects of nebivolol by interfering with CYP2D6 hepatic metabolism. Careful monitoring is advised. 10. Chloroquine increases the toxicity of nilotinib by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor the patient. 11. Chloroquine elevates the levels or effects of nortriptyline by inhibiting CYP2D6 hepatic metabolism. Additionally, it increases nortriptyline toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are required. 12. Co-administration of chloroquine and ofatumumab SC may enhance immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Consider the additive effects on the immune system and monitor closely. When transitioning therapies, account for the duration and mechanism of action of the previous treatment. 13. Chloroquine increases the toxicity of olanzapine by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor the patient. 14. Chloroquine and olaparib exhibit pharmacodynamic synergy, potentially increasing toxicity. Monitor closely and adjust therapy as needed. 15. Chloroquine raises the levels or effects of oliceridine by inhibiting CYP2D6 hepatic metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. If co-administration is necessary, reduce the frequency of oliceridine dosing and monitor for respiratory depression and sedation. Adjust subsequent doses accordingly. If the inhibitor is discontinued, consider increasing the oliceridine dosage until stable effects are achieved. Monitor for signs of opioid withdrawal. 16. Omaveloxolone reduces the levels or effects of chloroquine by decreasing systemic exposure to sensitive CYP2C8 substrates. Check prescribing information for potential dosage modifications and monitor closely. 17. Chloroquine increases the toxicity of ondansetron by prolonging the QTc interval. Exercise caution and monitor the patient. 18. Chloroquine and osilodrostat both prolong the QTc interval, increasing the risk of toxicity. Use caution and monitor the patient. 19. Chloroquine increases the toxicity of osimertinib by prolonging the QTc interval. Exercise caution and monitor the patient. 20. Oxaliplatin raises the levels or effects of chloroquine through an unspecified mechanism. Monitor for ECG changes, especially in patients receiving drugs known to prolong the QT interval. 21. Chloroquine increases the levels or effects of oxycodone by inhibiting CYP2D6 hepatic metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient. 22. Chloroquine elevates the levels or effects of oxymorphone by interfering with CYP2D6 hepatic metabolism. Careful monitoring is advised. 23. Chloroquine increases the toxicity of paliperidone by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor the patient. 24. Phenobarbital reduces chloroquine levels by inducing CYP3A4-mediated hepatic and intestinal metabolism. Monitor the patient closely. 25. Phenytoin decreases chloroquine levels by inducing CYP3A4 hepatic and intestinal metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient. 26. Potassium bicarbonate reduces chloroquine levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Separate doses by at least 4 hours and monitor closely. 27. Chloroquine increases the levels or effects of propafenone by inhibiting CYP2D6 hepatic metabolism. Additionally, it increases propafenone toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor the patient. 28. Chloroquine raises the levels or effects of propranolol by interfering with CYP2D6 hepatic metabolism. Careful monitoring is advised. 29. Chloroquine increases the toxicity of quetiapine by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor the patient. 30. Chloroquine increases the toxicity of ranolazine by prolonging the QTc interval. Exercise caution and monitor the patient.
